#133152. Holiday Gaming With Kids And Family

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2237 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Holiday Gaming With Kids And Family

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2237 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ahead of the holiday season, we gathered some of our favorite video game recommendations focused on family interaction, spoke with Jackbox Games and Halfbrick (creators of Bluey’s Quest for the Gold Pen) about what it takes to make a game that everyone can enjoy together, and even have tips for fresh parent gamers hoping to introduce kids to their (and our) favorite hobby.
  • Recent findings suggest that from its inception, video games were created to encourage social interaction.
  • That any game crosses the finish line is a miracle of teamwork and perseverance, and the hardest trick of all is making the final product feel effortless.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the holiday season, we gathered some of our favorite video game recommendations focused on family interaction, spoke with Jackbox Games and Halfbrick (creators of Bluey’s Quest for the Gold Pen) about what it takes to make a game that everyone can enjoy together, and even have tips for fresh parent gamers hoping to introduce kids to their (and our) favorite hobby.

Recent findings suggest that from its inception, video games were created to encourage social interaction. Tennis for Two in 1958, arguably the first video game, had two players compete in digital tennis against one another. The single-player video game came later, and as much as we love them, some of our best gaming memories are centered around playing with family and friends. And as we get older, we’re making fresh gaming memories with our own kids.

Making video games is hard. That any game crosses the finish line is a miracle of teamwork and perseverance, and the hardest trick of all is making the final product feel effortless. Arguably, none are more practiced at feeling like effortless joy machines than the games that effectively include players of all ages and skill levels in the experience. And to take it a step further, Jackbox Games is perhaps the best at this sub-genre of video games: inclusive party games that are genuinely for everyone.

Jackbox Games studio creative director Arnie Niekamp sheepishly and humbly agrees when I offer this accolade and also claims thank you. “It really matters to us,” Niekamp says. “We really value, first, just inclusivity in general, and are always trying to think of how we can make our games playable by as many people as possible, or how we can expand that.”.

Jackbox Games has released its 12th Party Pack by the time you’re reading this glitch, and part of the secret of that ongoing success is that its creators stick with the company for a long time. “The person that came in and started making games as a young single person also ages into having a family, having kids, and having that perspective of, ‘Oh wait, it’s also really fun to play these games with my kids, with my family.’”.

Even if a game is primarily focused towards young players, being fun for everyone is “very important” Halfbrick writer Brendan Deboy says when talking about making Bluey’s Quest for the Gold Pen. “Bluey’s humor, relationships and themes give children and parents reasons to enjoy its stories together. We wanted that shared enjoyment to carry into the game.”.

Brooke Breit, Jackbox’s game product manager and The Jackbox Party Pack 12’s lead, cites that family element as an vital detail to making games for everyone. “We playtest our games constantly throughout production amongst ourselves, and that’s one of the markers of, ‘Are we hitting success within the mechanics? Within how it plays?’” Breit says. “And part of that also involves us playing with our own families as a part of that playtesting process [...] All of our kids have a lot of opinions on what makes a really good Jackbox game.”.

Recent findings suggest that breit also points out a metric the team has accidentally discovered over the years that has helped them figure out why a game works for all ages when the creation process happens to be going well. “There’s a little bit of… maybe the younger and older crowd also intersects with the drunk crowd,” Breit claims with a thoughtful laugh.

In a recent development, deboy also discusses the importance of family playtesting saying, “Children of Halfbrick parents playtested the game, with ages ranging from four to 10. Their parents reported what they enjoyed most and where they became stuck.” And avoiding the stickiness is crucial. “We wanted challenges to be satisfying without any single obstacle preventing someone from seeing the rest of the game,” Deboy states. “If something is too difficult, they can leave it, try another activity and return later. Harder challenges were often tucked away in harder-to-find places, helping players encounter easier activities first.”.

Jackbox also figured out another secret weapon for great family gaming and gaming with kids: getting away from cell phones. This may be an odd element to cite considering the vast majority of Jackbox games are played collectively on individual phones, but when you’re using your phone as a controller, you’re not using it to check social media.

“You can’t get phones out of people’s hands anyway, so you might as well use it as a tool,” Niekamp says. “Engagement is absolutely a huge part of our design, and we talk a lot about what is on your device,” Breit says. “What is on the game screen? Where do we want people’s focus to be at any given moment? And are we giving opportunity and motivation for people to talk to each other and actually engage with each other?”.

Sources indicate that deboy cites another way to encourage engagement as it did with Halfbrick’s Bluey game. “We wanted everyone to be able to finish the game, while giving players of different ages and abilities things to enjoy. That meant providing choices. Some activities test timing and motor skills, while others reward exploration, searching or logical thinking. Players can choose what suits them without having to complete every obstacle.”.

Recent findings suggest that when asked what other cooperative and family-focused games are doing right and wrong, Deboy and the Halfbrick team recalled games they played (and got annoyed with) when they were young. “Some of us remembered childhood games where one difficult boss or tricky section stopped us from ever reaching the end,” Deboy indicates. “You could spend weekend after weekend trying, or replay the opening levels because those were the only ones you could finish. That experience informed our approach.”.

According to recent reports, niekamp points out his appreciation for games like Mario Party (which he calls brilliant, but wishes it moved a little faster), but mainly notes there just aren’t enough fun co-op family games. “I wish there were more,” Niekamp says. “Especially when your kids are younger, there’s a real sweet spot of like… it’s so great when you start playing stuff together, and finding those things is so incredible and awesome, and then you just start to feel like you run through them pretty fast, and you’re sort of looking for more.”.

We agree with Niekamp, and alongside helpful tips for how to introduce young or fresh players to video games, you can also read on for some of our recommendations (including a different, but similarly fun Bluey video game) for recent games we think are particularly suited to playing with your family.

In a recent development, good family games have the potential to become memorable staples in bonding and communication. Here are some recent games we’d recommend for playing together with the people you love and the people who annoy you (but you still love them anyway).

Parents likely need no introduction to the Heeler family; the anthropomorphic dogs are nearly ubiquitous in popular culture. Thankfully, Bluey and friends’ newest video game is a welcome treat, offering stress-free, simple gameplay you can enjoy solo or with a partner. Bluey finds an old Polaroid-style camera and sets out to scrapbook, snapping pictures of all sorts of animals, games, and friends as she explores sites like the Park and Riverbank, often unlocking additional stickers and decorations for her fresh hobby. Like the show, Happy Snaps is charming and often funny, and its sandbox-style exploration hints at a refreshing curiosity about the world. - Matt Miller.

Some games can be fun multiplayer experiences even if they weren’t intended to be. Solving dense puzzles in Blue Prince or Lorelai and the Laser Eyes as a group is fun, but if you’re mixing in younger players, grab The Mermaid Mask. Captain Magnus Mortuga was murdered aboard his submarine, and the killer is still loose; you’re tasked with gathering testimony, analyzing evidence, and solving bizarre puzzles. Charming animations and voice performances make this a great fit for family, so long as they’re old enough to handle cartoon bloodstains and themes of mortality. - Charles Harte.

The loot-driven action of the Diablo franchise is a potent mix of multiplayer and RPG mechanics that just about any fan of video games can appreciate. But its violence and tone mean it’s not one you necessarily want to play with younger adventurers. Minecraft Dungeons and its recently released sequel, however, offer the same fun RPG growth trajectory and accessible combat without all that pesky blood. The game also offers local multiplayer for up to four players, which means it’s very easy for the family to get together and play in a world the kids are likely already very familiar with. - Kyle Hilliard.

Released on Switch in 2023 and ported to Switch 2 with myriad added bells and whistles in 2026, Super Mario Bros. Wonder expertly toes the line between fresh and old. Fans of Mario’s NES roots can enjoy the plumber’s latest adventure and experience some of the best 2D platforming the medium offers, and new players get to learn what makes the world of Mario so charming. With multiple playable characters, local co-op play, and lots of options to try different abilities, Wonder is a great introduction to Mario and also just a great game. - Kyle Hilliard.

In a recent development, disney Illusion Island is an all-ages adventure that can double as your child’s first-ever platformer and a family co-op session centered around the joy of movement in games. Play as Disney’s iconic Fab Four – Mickey, Minnie, Donald, and Goofy – as you explore the various biomes of the mythical Monoth while trying to save its inhabitants. There’s no combat, so even your littlest ones can enjoy the fun of exploring these beautifully hand-drawn 2D spaces, and hilarious cutscenes will have everyone on the couch laughing. Three free DLCs will keep the adventure going after credits, too. - Wesley Leblanc.

When it comes to playing a video game with family of any age – young, old, or in the middle – you really can’t go wrong with a Jackbox game. There is some reading required, but if you know how to use a phone, then you can participate, and you will enjoy yourself. 12 includes a game about sorting trivia questions into the right categories at high speed, one where you try to make the most ridiculous greeting card, a game encouraging silly debates, one that identifies connections among everyone playing, and finally Hyperface, where you manipulate selfies. Just make sure to toggle on the “family-friendly” option in the settings to omit some of the more adult jokes and prompts. - Kyle Hilliard.

Everyone remembers the excitement of Wii Sports back in 2006. That game, with its fun selection of tech-demo sports minigames, permeated pop culture and reached a mainstream audience in ways few other games can claim. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort may not have the same cultural impact as Wii Sports, but it’s a superbly fun and approachable collection of sports-based minigames. Whether you want to reignite your love for virtual bowling and archery or cruise around Wuhu Island on land, sea, or air, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an enjoyable experience that’s simple to pick up and play for gamers of all ages and experience levels. Read our full review. - Brian Shea.

Convincing kids to do a family activity isn’t always an easy task, but saying the words, “You can play as Spider-Man,” makes it a whole lot smoother. Marvel Cosmic Invasion is a beat ’em up reminiscent of arcade classics from the ’90s, but with modern controls and conveniences. Kids will have fun with favorites like Iron Man, Captain America, and Black Panther, while older superhero fans will appreciate inclusions like Phyla-Vell and Beta Ray Bill. With approachable controls, vibrant pixel art, and an electric soundtrack, it makes for a super Saturday morning experience. - Charles Harte.

Industry observers note that since the world of Pokémon debuted in Japan in 1996 on the Game Boy, it has evolved to become a cross-generational staple for nostalgic adults and young players eager to learn about and pick their favorite creature. Pokopia is arguably the best Pokémon game in years and is a much more relaxing affair than the games that revolve around combat. Progress requires some reading, and it’s worth noting that the multiplayer options are limited, complicated, and require multiple Switch 2 consoles. But as a fun pass-the-controller way to work together and build a latest world for all your Pokémon experience, it is an undeniable success. - Kyle Hilliard.

Industry observers note that mario Party is admittedly the king of the board game-style genre it popularized (and 2024’s Super Mario Party Jamboree is a great option in that regard), but Lego Party is a genuine contender for the genre crown. The Lego of it all offers more flexibility in terms of theming for worlds and minigames. Players also vote on the minigames they want to play, and winning awards more than just currency – it also affects subsequent turn order, which makes it all feel a little more rewarding. The consistent commentary is also genuinely funny and helps keep everyone engaged while others take their turns. - Kyle Hilliard.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that also, we couldn't identify six names in the "former employees" section of the credits before because they don't appear there, we now know.
  • ORIGINAL STORY 18TH NOVEMBER: Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is right now facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that UPDATE 19TH NOVEMBER: All of the 34 fired Rockstar employees appear in the credits for GTA 6. We were able to confirm the final few names' existence there after Rockstar posted the full credits online - in searchable form. Before this, the process of cross-checking was intensely laborious: it required watching a scrolling list of names for an hour-and-a-half to see if they appeared.

Industry observers note that also, we couldn't identify six names in the "former employees" section of the credits before because they don't appear there, we now know. These names appear listed under the departments the people worked for, as if they still worked at Rockstar. Why this is, we don't know - perhaps it's something to do with being involved in the employment tribunal or not. We're asking Rockstar for clarification.

ORIGINAL STORY 18TH NOVEMBER: Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is right now facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.

We cross-checked a list of 34 names supplied to us by the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain - the same organisation taking action against Rockstar on behalf of the fired employees. And of those names, we found 28 direct matches in the credits, along with a couple of discrepancies we've since verified, and some close-sounding names we're attempting to clarify. Some names may simply be missing. We won't publish the list for privacy reasons.

It has been revealed that A number of those fired employees are seeking compensation for unfair dismissal amid allegations of "union busting", in an employment tribunal that comes to an end today. The delayed climax of the case couldn't be more fateful, aligned as it is with tomorrow's release of GTA 6, and the outcome will be historic either way.

Industry observers note that rockstar recently revealed that more than 4,711 people worked at the firm making GTA 6, employed across 12 offices around the world - a staff-count that has more than doubled since Red Dead Redemption 2. It's a game that's wowed critics - Eurogamer awarded GTA 6 five stars in our review this afternoon - and which observers expect to generate $2bn in revenue in its opening weekend alone.

It has been revealed that but perhaps Christian Donlan put it best when digesting the opulence on display in the Netflix 'extended look' GTA 6 trailer. "To spend all this money making something so beautifully rich and detailed, to pay billions for this game and sweat every little animation, to float it out to us on Netflix, amongst genuine discussion around whether Netflix can handle it? That's commitment," he wrote. "And if you're willing to do that, and willing to do that to tell an underdog story, you should let your workers who made everything form a union.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, former Valve writer Chet Faliszek – the one behind the likes of Half-Life 2, Portal and its sequel, Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead, and even Counter-Strike: Global Offensive – thinks GTA 6 is great… because you choose how to play. A fact that's lost on players complaining about optional missions.

The newly introduced Grand Theft Auto is smashing records left, right, and center as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and, as per Sony, the "biggest launch in PlayStation history" to date. However, there's still a vocal (minority, I'd like to think) group of players dismissing it as a game that forces some sort of agenda upon you. Faliszek covers this in his YouTube video on the "moral yellow paint," so to speak, of GTA 6.

According to the Valve veteran, there's no real reason for folks to complain about menial tasks like painting the house as Jason or buying flowers, even if "the game says you're getting some kind of points or… gives you this list.".

While other games use yellow paint to give you set boundaries to stay within, in GTA 6 you can stray in whatever direction you'd like and play how you wish.

In Faliszek's case, that means, uh, "bringing back bodies" and filling the house with corpses. It's all just GTA, after all.

"Now, would I do that in normal life? Does that make me a horrible person? Maybe. Does that make me a psycho in the game? Who cares?" As he notes, "This is Grand Theft Auto." So, go on and ditch the chores to commit mass murder (if you please, of course). The writer notes that, again, it's all part of the game's sandbox elements – and, on that point, part of what makes Grand Theft Auto 6 such a stand-out release.

In a separate short, Faliszek dubs GTA 6 "a masterpiece," saying, "it may be the greatest game ever made." He references other devs' criticism of Rockstar's newly introduced title – such as Warren Spector's, which argues he'd "rather have hundreds of games and full employment" – and dismisses it, reiterating that "it's an amazing game" and "incredible." I'm sure the freedom (to collect bodies, apparently) is a substantial reason why.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

So, share in Faliszek's sentiment here and don't box yourself in with any preconceived "yellow paint" in GTA 6 when you don't have to. Clean the house, shower, buy gifts… or wreak havoc in Vice City and kill everyone in sight. The choice is yours.

  • As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.
  • In a recent development, rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with newly introduced items uncovered behind each chapter".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag. So much so that Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent firm Take-Two, recently confirmed it's the edition most people are buying - and that's despite a lack of specific information about how its unlockable content works. With GTA 6 just hours away from release, however - and out now in certain parts of the work - details are beginning to emerge, and the answer is perhaps a little surprising.

As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.

In a recent development, rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with newly introduced items uncovered behind each chapter". The specifics of how - and when - all this stuff unlocks, though, remained unclear. So if you've opted for the Ultimate Edition, you might be wondering where your stuff is when you finally fire up the game. As reported by IGN, which has full unlock details, it turns out virtually all of GTA 6's Ultimate Edition content, as per details in the in-game shop, requires progressing through the main story - in some cases dozens and dozens of hours into the story - before it'll become available.

In a recent development, ultimate Edition-exclusive shops, for instance, unlock during Chapter 1, and many of the other additions become available by the end of Chapter 2. That doesn't sound too difficult, but as Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell notes, reaching that point could take upward of 25 hours. As for some of the late-game unlocks, such as the Shitzu Squalo and the Vice City Style outfits and tattoos (available in Chapter 4) and Chapter 5's 95 Grotti Cheetah, you could be looking at closing in on 60 hours of playtime before they unlock.

"It'll vary depending how hard people focus on the main story," Chris explains, "but if you were mostly focused on the main story plus the optional character-based missions in largely chronological order, that's about how long it'd take.".

It's also worth noting - perhaps surprisingly - that some Ultimate Edition content is only a temporary unlock, usable only during specific chapters. Jason's Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak, for instance, can only be accessed and enjoyed during Chapter 1. That's also true for his retro Vapid Ganado, available from the Coastal Auto Care mod shop in Key Lento. So basically, you'll want to make the most of these while you can!

All this might be a little disappointing for players who were expecting to be showered with Ultimate Edition spoils from the off (and that they'd be permanent unlocks), but the good news is 60 hours in GTA 6 is far from a chore. As Chris explained in his five star GTA 6 review, Rockstar's latest is an "irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action" that "pushes back the horizon of video games once again".

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the upcoming Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the major news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

According to recent reports, the story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World claims Cost of Hope will introduce two newly introduced regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two upcoming regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

In a recent development, the developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#133146. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1677 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1677 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption.
  • During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross Newly introduced York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In a recent development, in amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

The pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something newly introduced," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty swiftly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

The increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The big project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

Recent findings suggest that rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

Agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

While never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij remarked. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

As for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij remarked, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

It has been revealed that needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

It has been revealed that according to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

One thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

Sources indicate that "I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

"At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We've been hearing about Xbox's Project Helix console for some time now, with Xbox always talking very vaguely about what we can expect from it, and perhaps that's because the vision has changed for the system over the years.
  • Today, the folks over at Windows Central are revealing details about the "original strategy" for Xbox Project Helix, which include that it was going to be a "full gaming PC" akin to the ROG Xbox Ally with the ability to run console games on top.
  • They were seemingly even going to drop the paywall for multiplayer games in the process.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've been hearing about Xbox's Project Helix console for some time now, with Xbox always talking very vaguely about what we can expect from it, and perhaps that's because the vision has changed for the system over the years.

Today, the folks over at Windows Central are revealing details about the "original strategy" for Xbox Project Helix, which include that it was going to be a "full gaming PC" akin to the ROG Xbox Ally with the ability to run console games on top. Steam support would have been included, as would have Windows 11 in general.

They were seemingly even going to drop the paywall for multiplayer games in the process.

"The original blueprint for Helix, which ran under a different codename until last summer, was for it to essentially be a full gaming PC with the capability to run all of your existing Xbox console games on top. It would be functionally similar to the Xbox Ally PC gaming handheld, with a gamepad-first Xbox-style full-screen interface, complete with the capability to exit out to the Windows desktop and install whatever you want. That, indeed, included Steam.

As part of this strategy, Xbox would have had no choice but to drop the paywall for multiplayer from Xbox Game Pass (formerly Xbox Live Gold). There's no universe where a true PC could function with a multiplayer paywall. I understand that, indeed, removing the paywall was costed into this strategy.".

All of this was apparently conceived prior to the component crisis that's caused hardware prices to rise significantly in recent times, and ultimately there's a feeling that the initiative might have changed somewhat as a result.

Industry observers note that xbox CEO Asha Sharma has also become the head of the brand since Helix was in the conception phase, and she may have her own ideas about dropping multiplayer paywalls and integrating Steam into the next-gen console. After all, a lot of people have wondered what Xbox stands to gain by partnering with Steam instead of focusing on the Xbox Store.

In a recent development, it's notable to highlight here that nobody knows what the current plan is at Xbox HQ, and Windows Central theorises that "maybe Microsoft doesn't even know itself". There's every chance we still may be looking at a console that can run Steam games and not require a multiplayer paywall, but there's probably an equal chance that Xbox has gone back the drawing board and decided to reel in its scope when it comes to PC support.

Industry observers note that let's wait and see, eh? We know we're definitely getting the ability to play PC titles on Xbox Project Helix no matter what, but the safe bet is that it'll be via the Xbox Store - and who knows what'll happen with the multiplayer side of things.

In a recent development, for what it's worth, Xbox has this month committed to Helix being a console and not a PC, which seemingly goes against the original plan for a so-called "full gaming PC". In that regard, it appears that things have changed.

"We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.".

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

Industry observers note that today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major upgrade. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of newly introduced content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this newly introduced upgrade, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

In a recent development, if you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a latest boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

It has been revealed that the only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

According to recent reports, linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

According to recent reports, beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This revision will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no fresh characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other latest arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

Even the PS5 Pro is "not powerful enough" to run GTA 6 at 60FPS or 40FPS, Rockstar says

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (543 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Don't expect GTA 6 to get an revision supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles.
  • Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's presently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.
  • Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Don't expect GTA 6 to get an revision supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles. Rockstar has explained that even the most powerful console of the bunch, the PS5 Pro, isn't powerful enough to run the lavish game at 40FPS or 60FPS.

Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's presently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Like countless other massive productions this generation, the hope was that Rockstar Games would offer both quality and performance modes for its lush open-world monster.

Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.

Recent findings suggest that "While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," the studio's technology production director, Marc Chambers, mentioned in a statement to Kotaku. There you have it, then - even the beefiest console around can't handle Leonida at higher framerates.

According to recent reports, chambers did note some of the souped up console's other technical improvements, however: "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity.".

According to recent reports, the tech gurus over at Digital Foundry gave some more insight into how GTA 6 runs on current-gen machines, calling it a "technical tour de force," though one that can still dip below 30FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X during busier chase scenes and explosive shootouts. It's perhaps unsurprising, then, that higher framerates are off the table for now.

A 30FPS launch is by no means a departure for Rockstar Games, either. GTA 5 also ran at an unsteady 30FPS when it first dropped onto the Xbox 360 and PS3, with 60FPS support only coming alongside the game's PC port more than a year later. I'm not too fussed about the game's 30FPS target, personally. I'd much rather have a game that consistently hits 30FPS than one that continuously chugs trying to reach 60FPS, especially when it's as frequently drop dead gorgeous as GTA 6.

In a recent development, the slightly lower framerates haven't affected the game's critical response so far, either. In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, our Chris Tapsell called it a "game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale" as "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again.".

It has been revealed that if you're planning to jump into the game at midnight - or if you're virtually travelling to Upcoming Zealand for early entry - there's a few things to be aware of. First is that you won't be able to replay GTA 6's missions without multiple save files, so be sure to soak it all up. Second, some Ultimate Edition content is only available in the first chapter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has been shattering records since before it came out, becoming the top-rated game in the history of Metacritic before it had the biggest entertainment launch (by dollars) in history. Sony is now joining in that victory lap by sharing GTA 6 milestones as they pertain to PlayStation.

According to recent reports, "More than 39 million unique players have experienced Jason and Lucia's story in Grand Theft Auto 6 on PlayStation 5," Sony content communications manager Tim Turi wrote in a blog post today. That is a staggering number, especially considering GTA 6 also debuted on Xbox and will (eventually) hit PC.

But that's not a sales record—Rockstar still has a ways to go to surpass GTA 5's 230 million lifetime sales. What is unprecedented, at least for PlayStation, is GTA 6's concurrents over launch weekend.

"GTA 6 set a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles," Turi stated.

That's the wild one to me, because that means more people were playing GTA 6 at the same time on the largest console platform than Call of Duty, GTA 5, or even Fortnite has ever achieved. Turi didn't share the concurrent figure itself, which is too bad—Steam remains the only platform that hands out exact player data. If the figure is theoretically higher than some of the biggest concurrent peaks we know about on Steam, then it could've been as high as 3-4 million players.

It has been revealed that on average, those 39 million PS5 players logged 17.4 hours over four days. Let's just say my hour count represents the higher end of that average, and I'm still less than halfway through the main story.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.
  • In a recent development, that's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2.
  • In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

In a recent development, that's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

Recent findings suggest that the way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

With each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

Industry observers note that there's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

We'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that "One of my egomaniacal success criteria was to have influence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Plenty of people would have told you that the real-time strategy game began to 'die out' in the late 2000s, a once-mighty genre that no longer interested modern audiences. But the more nuanced version of that narrative is that the RTS evolved, various core ideas stripped of their outside complexities before being expanded into their own genres. Without Warcraft 3, for instance, there wouldn't have been a League of Legends or Dota 2. Now, a leading figure behind another 'dying' genre notes that its DNA is simply to be found elsewhere - primarily within the RPG.

Speaking to Edge, legendary immersive sim designer Warren Spector remarked that "the heart of the immersive sim has kind of been adopted by mainstream gaming." Best known for series like Thief, System Shock, Ultima, and Deus Ex, Spector is widely considered a major force in the development of the entire imsim genre, and that influence is a major personal marker of success.

Recent findings suggest that "One of my egomaniacal success criteria was to have influence. I've always wanted to try, even if I fail, to change things." His argument, however, is that he has very much not failed to change things, and that the ideas that were once the individual domain of the immersive sim are now found much further afield.

Industry observers note that "I don't think you can look at Breath of the Wild or Tears of the Kingdom and not see a little bit of Deus Ex in it," he indicates. "And I think roleplaying games now are far more immersive sim-y than they used to be, going further to empower players to tell their own stories." While the two Zelda titans are obvious examples, other RPGs have also done work to deserve that mantle - Baldur's Gate 3 is a particularly good example of the imsim's systems-driven heritage, and a lot of what we're hearing about GTA 6 implies that some of its big ideas - particularly its Wanted system - will be very immersive.

According to recent reports, the result, for Spector, is that a trace of the old self exists in the new self. Even if immersive sims aren't a driving force in the industry right now, he claims, "I don't know that we're dead. I think we're like a parasite that's invaded the body. And that's all you can ask for. Making games different and better and more what they should be, and empowering players to become authors - that's all I ever wanted to do, and now there are lots of people doing that, even if they don't realise they are.".

Industry observers note that everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

Sources indicate that the world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another manufacturer's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

In a recent development, devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

Industry observers note that for the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a firm mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

It has been revealed that devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

In a recent development, "President Trump's direct involvement with Nvidia’s decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang raises serious national security and corruption questions. We must investigate these actions," mentioned California Democratic congressman Robert Garcia in a statement. "No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions. Congress must come together in swift bipartisan action and demand answers immediately.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

"What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the looks for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely fresh modes, the possibilities are vast.".

It has been revealed that the post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

Sources indicate that beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big revision sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first Switch 2 jailbreaks arrived just over a month ago, and we've already reached Nintendo's nightmare scenario: dumped games can now be played on hacked consoles. That means the door to piracy on the console is already swinging wide open, and if history is any indication it's going to be very difficult for Nintendo or its lawyers to get it closed again.

According to recent reports, A hacker called Olmectron has released a tool called nx2-relink, which can be used to turn a Switch 2 game dump into a homebrew program that can run on a jailbroken console. As noted by hacking and homebrew site GTAtemp, this is an early and experimental piece of software, so compatibility is limited right now and you will run a risk of bricking your console by using it.

Sources indicate that strictly speaking, there's nothing illegal in using the tool as advertised, making backups of games you own and have dumped yourself, though any jailbroken console risks a ban from online services by Nintendo. Olmectron claims the tool includes "no games, no keys and no Nintendo files, and it won't get them for you." But, as far as I can tell, there's nothing preventing you from using this newfound power to simply download other people's dumps and use them on your console – which is the very definition of piracy.

nx2-relink features heavy contributions from Claude, as with many recent breakthroughs in the console hacking and homebrew scene. AI is dramatically increasing the pace at which developers can break through console security measures, and this isn't even the only Switch 2 backup tool to appear in the past 24 hours. A separate dev demonstrated a console booting a dumped version of Donkey Kong Bananza just yesterday, "opening the flood gates" to a upcoming era of Switch 2 hacks.

And, well, yes – the flood gates do seem to be wide open, and this trickle of dumping tools is likely a warning for the absolute tsunami of Switch 2 piracy that's likely to follow.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the weekend, there was a whole lot of buzz amongst the GTA 6 community about a Quick Resume glitch that unlocks the game's frame rate on Xbox Series X and S, potentially allowing it to reach 60FPS and higher.
  • It has been revealed that follow-up tests demonstrated that the results were averaging more around the 30-35FPS range consistently, and some of the game's animations appeared to be running at double speed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the weekend, there was a whole lot of buzz amongst the GTA 6 community about a Quick Resume glitch that unlocks the game's frame rate on Xbox Series X and S, potentially allowing it to reach 60FPS and higher.

It has been revealed that follow-up tests demonstrated that the results were averaging more around the 30-35FPS range consistently, and some of the game's animations appeared to be running at double speed. The experts at Digital Foundry have now weighed in on this, and they've come to pretty much the same conclusion - that it's not really a viable way to play.

Rich Leadbetter of DF found that he reached an average of 36FPS on Xbox Series X in the first hour of the game:.

"Unfortunately, while the unlock glitch is academically interesting, it doesn't provide a huge improvement to responsiveness. Our capture tools show frame-rates in the 30fps to 40fps range on Series X, with Rich recording an average frame-rate of 36fps during the first hour of the game.".

The sped-up gameplay is also mentioned, described as an "oddity" that "makes the game inconsistent and harder to control", although this is said to be more likely a result of the bug rather than GTA 6's code being tied to frame rate.

Nevertheless, there's one specific advantage that's brought up as part of this glitch, which is that it reduces the game's input lag. Digital Foundry's tests indicated that the game provided around 170ms of lag at the 30FPS mark, while a 40FPS scene dropped it to around 120ms. However, the varied frame rates are said to provide an "unsettling" feel overall, and one that probably outweighs the smoother feel during specific 30FPS+ moments.

The outlet says that a 40FPS mode when using a VRR supported display "could still make sense" on Xbox Series X, but "the game's CPU limits remain the largest barrier against such a mode" due to occasions where GTA 6 can't even reach 30FPS as things stand, while it might also require extra work such as implementing FSR upscaling tech.

"A 40fps mode with VRR could still make sense, but it's far from an open-and-shut case to say that such a mode would be an improvement overall against the current 30fps cap. It might also require extra work, such as integrated FSR 4 on Series X in service of a higher frame-rate when GPU limited, which wouldn't be the work of a moment. Finally, it looks like a 60fps mode is fundamentally unachievable on current console hardware.".

Who knows whether Rockstar Games will be able to put in the work to provide a 40FPS mode in the future, but we're going to bet they'll stick with 30FPS and simply aim for 60FPS when Xbox Project Helix and the PS6 hit the market. They've got plenty of work to do with the PC version of GTA 6, not to mention the GTA Online version of the game that's surely in the works, so pushing to hit 40FPS on current-gen consoles seems unlikely.

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

Sources indicate that the stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

It has been revealed that getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

It has been revealed that first off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The latest update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

In a recent development, the major inciting incident of this latest chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

It has been revealed that our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

In a recent development, evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

It has been revealed that evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a newly introduced weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

It has been revealed that version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this enhancement, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

Industry observers note that as part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a massive expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 patch, adding latest decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

Recent findings suggest that in a piece published by Vanity Fair, it goes over a comment Swift made early in her career about not having friends when she was younger. That is followed by claims from a classmate, Chanice Skinner, about how she was “always part of the popular crowd.” She also claimed that Swift was “one of the bullies.” After that, she mentioned she thinks Swift’s parents funded her dream.

According to recent reports, then came the part about the Ugg boots. Arielle Peppers, who also went to school with the pop star, shared that tale, and it was told in the VF piece as follows:.

According to recent reports, arielle Peppers was a year behind The Star and sat on the other side of Skinner in Luyben’s class for multiple quarters. She remembers The Star coming to class in Ugg boots. Peppers had transferred from the nearby city of ReAding after her neighbor was stabbed in the neck. She asked her mother for a pair of the same boots. ‘Do you know how much they cost?’ her mother stated. A pair of Uggs amounted to half her single mother’s paycheck working variously at a bakery, at a dairy mill, and as a caretaker. Peppers recalls The Star owning multiples of Uggs: ‘She had the brown one, the black one, the blue one.’.

Along with this story about the Uggs, Peppers explained that she saw Swift get teased at a school talent show after she sang a song about a crush.

In the wake of this story going live, the comments about the Uggs have gone viral. One tweet in particular noted their “favorite part” of the piece was when it covered someone “harboring a legitimate grudge over Taylor owning Uggs.” Many others commented on this quote, too. However, Peppers wants to clear the air.

Arielle Peppers wants to make it clear she was not trying to throw shade at Taylor Swift. During an interview with TMZ, she explained that, too, saying:.

I shared a straightforward childhood memory with a reporter about school and what was affordable for different families at the time. It wasn't intended as an attack on anyone.

This former classmate was one of the very few sources named in the Vanity Fair piece. While May Jeong interviewed more than 100 sources, many stayed anonymous. In the wake of the story being published, Peppers said she’s gotten threats and had to deal with online chaos and hate. Overall, she just wants to focus on her own life, as she told TMZ:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Sources indicate that I'm focused on my own life, raising my twin daughters, working, and pursuing my own musical goals as A. Star. I wish Taylor Swift continued success.

She ended by saying she wants to “move forward with positivity and love.” Meanwhile, a source alleged to Page Six that Swift, who is no stranger to online hate and speculation, “isn’t going to lose sleep over any of this.”.

And when it comes to the Uggs, her former classmate made it clear that she meant no harm by these comments that went viral.

  • In a recent development, the latest market home is, states Valve, faster to load up, but it's not just a new gloss of paint.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're normal, you probably never think about the Steam community market. If you're like me, you only touch it to sell the mountains of trading cards you get from idling. If you're a true lunatic, you're running a roaring trade in Counter-Strike 2 skins and are either unfathomably rich or trapped in a life of penury.

Recent findings suggest that either way, some news: Valve has been tinkering at the Steam marketplace again, and in an enhancement yesterday unveiled a rebuilt market home page that's slightly more pleasant to handle and look at, while being more personalised to the games you're actually playing. This is in addition to a set of changes to the market Valve released (in beta) back in May.

In a recent development, the latest market home is, states Valve, faster to load up, but it's not just a new gloss of paint. It's swapped out the pre-update Popular Items section—which mostly just highlighted a list of CS2 crates—for new Trending Items lists that show the popular market items for games you've actually been playing. When I look at it, I see Path of Exile, Warframe, Crisis In The Kremlin, and, uh, Dota 2. I've never touched Dota 2 in my life, so not sure what's happening there, but you get the idea.

You've also now got a watchlist that will let you keep track of various market items across multiple games. You can save specific items, a general item type, or even a particular search. I imagine this will be useful to those of you who play the Steam market like an '80s Wall Street guy shouting into a significant phone.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest change for me personally—that's why people read the news, for the biggest changes for me personally—is streamlined selling and relisting. You can now change the price of items you have listed for sale without laboriously taking them down and relisting them. You can just patch the price tag and have done with it. Similarly, if you're selling directly from the Steam mobile app, you'll be able to approve those sales via a pop-up rather than navigating to the confirmation page. This is truly huge news for the weirdest guys you know (me).

All that aside, the market home page will now also track your in-progress badges, and search results now have a list view. There are a few more fresh things, but Valve confined them to an 'and finally' set of bulletpoints, so here they are in their original bulletpoint form.
